title: Hey! Any advice on how I could use AI to create 2D animations for my environments? I’ve got a few ideas in mind!
author: wacomlover
selftext:
Hi,

I want to create some animations for my backgrounds. Imagine, for example, a 2D view of a little town where I want to create animations of a curtain blowing in the wind, etc. These are the kinds of things I would like to be able to generate and integrate into my game.

I was thinking about using MiniMax H3, providing the background as a reference and generating an animation of the curtain. Then, I could use SAM 2 for segmentation (I assume some cleanup would be needed) and do a final pass with another model to consolidate the result for use in my game (it has some LoRAs).

On the other hand, I've come across a tool called Velorn, which is an AI video editor that might be useful, although I'm not sure about it yet.

What do you think? Do you think this approach could yield good results? Have you tried anything similar in the past with good results?

Thanks in advance!

comments.author: Ok-Way-9449
comments.body: Is the view of the curtain inside a room or outside looking at it.  Post a screen shot of where you want the curtains blowing in the wind.  IKt woul give everyone a bettre Idea on how to help you.

comments.author: ThePubRelic
comments.body: Just make the curtain another object placed ontop of the window that is affected by a wind shader that creates a 'heat' map that walks down from the pivot (top of the curtain) to decide the strength of the wind. Your curtain can then be a simple png generated by probably gpt, unless you want pixle art then I suggest claude.
